Phase 5 — Hydrogel rheology and printing-context exploratory analysis¶

This notebook is Phase 5 of the Open Materials Data Pipeline for Hydrogel Bioink Design project.

Phase 5 uses the verified Phase 4 evidence layer to ask a narrower and more useful question:

What descriptive rheology and image-metadata patterns can be explored without turning candidate filename relationships into confirmed physical-sample, formulation, printing-run or image links?

This is an exploratory analysis checkpoint, not a machine-learning checkpoint. The purpose is to create interpretable summaries and figures while preserving the scientific limits established in Phases 1–4.

The notebook is designed for a fresh Jupyter session:

  1. save the notebook;
  2. close Jupyter;
  3. reopen the notebook later;
  4. select the documented Python kernel;
  5. choose Restart Kernel;
  6. choose Run All Cells;
  7. expect the full workflow to run from top to bottom without hidden state.

Extended visualisation edition: keeps the original seven plots and adds a worksheet-level, QC-aware, rheology-mechanics and image-metadata visualisation atlas. Outputs appear inline and are saved as PNG files in data/processed/hydrogel_rheology_and_printing_context_analysis/figures/.

Kernel setup: from the selected Jupyter kernel run %pip install -r requirements-phase5.txt (if in the project root), then Restart Kernel → Run All Cells. Do not use an unrelated polymer-tg kernel. See the accompanying Phase 5 guide for Windows steps.

Important for Windows/Anaconda: Phase 5 v3 saves all 25 PNG figures but displays only four inline previews. Browse data/processed/hydrogel_rheology_and_printing_context_analysis/phase5_figure_gallery.html to see all visualisations. If a run remains Busy, check phase5_execution_progress.log in that directory. The last SECTION START or FIGURE START without a matching FINISHED line locates the blockage. No package manager runs during Run All.

v4 environment fix: The screenshot of the Windows hydrogel-bioink kernel shows that Matplotlib is absent. The pre-flight below attempts to install only missing Matplotlib with the Python interpreter running this notebook. The installer is bounded (150 seconds), prints progress and saves a local installer log; when Matplotlib is already installed, it makes no package-manager calls. It then tests headless figure rendering. If installation cannot finish (e.g. blocked internet or corporate proxy), a short manual Anaconda Prompt command is given instead of an unbounded Busy kernel. Your original scientific analysis, 25 PNG figures and four inline previews are retained.

Scientific boundaries for Phase 5¶

The Phase 4 outputs made the analysis possible, but they did not solve every scientific problem. Phase 5 therefore follows these rules:

  • Rheology points are treated as measurement points nested inside worksheets, not as independent formulations.
  • Filename-stem matching is treated as candidate evidence only, not as confirmed physical sample identity.
  • The source token mPas remains unresolved. Apparent viscosity is plotted in its source token rather than converted to Pa·s.
  • Image metadata can be summarised, but the actual image pixels are not inspected in this phase.
  • Shape labels, ink labels, irradiation intensity and SPS annotations are metadata fields, not automatically print-quality labels.
  • No predictive model, target label or training set is created here.
  • QC warnings are retained and reported rather than silently removed.

This sounds strict, but it is the useful kind of strict. It stops a pretty plot from quietly becoming a claim the source data never earned.

Data-science and polymer concepts used in this notebook¶

Exploratory data analysis describes distributions, ranges, missingness, grouping structure and possible patterns. It does not by itself prove causation or prediction readiness.

Measurement hierarchy matters because a rheology curve contains repeated points from one acquisition. Treating every point as an independent material would inflate the apparent amount of evidence.

Record linkage remains a source of uncertainty. A software join or matched filename can support review, but it is not the same as a verified material history.

Hydrogel rheology needs measurement context. Viscosity depends on shear rate and may show shear-thinning. Storage modulus G′ and loss modulus G″ describe elastic and viscous contributions under oscillatory test conditions. These quantities should be interpreted with strain, frequency, temperature and acquisition context attached.

Printing context is broader than rheology. Nozzle geometry, pressure, speed, crosslinking, construct design, irradiation, and image quality can matter. This dataset has some image metadata, but Phase 5 does not claim a validated printability target.

Start-up verification — install missing Matplotlib into the active kernel (v4)¶

This step addresses the error reported on Windows: Missing Python packages in this selected Jupyter kernel: matplotlib. It uses sys.executable to ensure that installation targets the Python interpreter actually running the notebook, not another Python installation.

  • If Matplotlib is already installed and importable, nothing is installed.
  • If Matplotlib is absent, the notebook attempts a single bounded binary-wheel installation using pip; it does not launch conda or wait indefinitely. Progress is printed and the installation log is saved.
  • If installation cannot be completed, the notebook stops with manual Anaconda Prompt instructions rather than silently skipping any graphs.
  • After installation, a tiny rendering test verifies that Matplotlib can generate PNG output using the non-interactive Agg backend.

Important: First-time installation needs internet access. The automated bootstrap cannot guarantee that a corporate firewall, proxy, locked-down environment or unsupported Python version will allow the installation. The one-time Anaconda Prompt alternative is in the accompanying guide.

# Phase 5 v4: bounded, kernel-specific Matplotlib installation + real render test.
# Does not run conda; does not reinstall packages that can already be imported.
# Do not copy this cell to unrelated environments without reviewing the dependency policy.
import importlib
import importlib.util
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path

ACTIVE_PYTHON = Path(sys.executable).resolve()
print('Selected Jupyter Python interpreter:', ACTIVE_PYTHON, flush=True)
print('Matplotlib setup: detecting packages.', flush=True)

# Select headless plotting BEFORE any import of matplotlib.pyplot.
os.environ['MPLBACKEND'] = 'Agg'

CORE_REQUIREMENTS = ('numpy', 'pandas', 'IPython')
missing_core = [p for p in CORE_REQUIREMENTS if importlib.util.find_spec(p) is None]
if missing_core:
    raise RuntimeError(
        'Core packages missing from the selected kernel: ' + ', '.join(missing_core) + '\n'
        'Use Anaconda Prompt to run:\n'
        '  conda activate hydrogel-bioink\n'
        '  conda install -c conda-forge numpy pandas ipython ipykernel matplotlib\n'
        'Restart the kernel before running all cells again.'
    )

# This is the only automatic package installation the notebook will attempt.
if importlib.util.find_spec('matplotlib') is None:
    if importlib.util.find_spec('pip') is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            'Matplotlib and pip are both missing from the active Jupyter interpreter.\n'
            'Use Anaconda Prompt: conda activate hydrogel-bioink\n'
            'conda install -c conda-forge matplotlib\n'
            'Then restart the kernel and Run All.'
        )
    # Avoid writing the log to a protected or unavailable project directory.
    try:
        INSTALL_LOG = Path.cwd() / 'phase5_matplotlib_install.log'
        with INSTALL_LOG.open('w', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
            handle.write('Phase 5 Matplotlib installation log\n')
    except OSError:
        INSTALL_LOG = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / 'phase5_matplotlib_install.log'

    install_command = [
        str(ACTIVE_PYTHON), '-m', 'pip', 'install',
        '--disable-pip-version-check', '--no-input', '--only-binary=:all:',
        '--retries', '1', '--timeout', '15', 'matplotlib',
    ]
    print('Matplotlib missing; attempting a ONE-TIME installation in this kernel.', flush=True)
    print('Installation log:', INSTALL_LOG, flush=True)
    MAX_INSTALL_SECONDS = 150
    start_install = time.monotonic()
    exit_code = None
    next_report = 15
    with INSTALL_LOG.open('a', encoding='utf-8') as install_output:
        try:
            child = subprocess.Popen(install_command, stdout=install_output,
                                     stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f'Cannot launch pip from {ACTIVE_PYTHON}: {exc}\n'
                'In Anaconda Prompt run: conda activate hydrogel-bioink\n'
                'conda install -c conda-forge matplotlib'
            ) from exc
        while True:
            exit_code = child.poll()
            if exit_code is not None:
                break
            elapsed_install = time.monotonic() - start_install
            if elapsed_install >= MAX_INSTALL_SECONDS:
                child.kill()
                child.wait()
                tail = INSTALL_LOG.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')[-2000:]
                raise RuntimeError(
                    'Matplotlib pip installation exceeded 150 seconds and was stopped.\n'
                    f'Log: {INSTALL_LOG}\nLast pip messages:\n{tail}\n'
                    'Use Anaconda Prompt outside Jupyter:\n'
                    '  conda activate hydrogel-bioink\n'
                    '  conda install -c conda-forge matplotlib\n'
                    'Restart the kernel and Run All afterward.'
                )
            # Keep the notebook visibly alive; do not present a silent Busy kernel.
            if elapsed_install >= next_report:
                print(f'Matplotlib installation in progress: {elapsed_install:.0f}s / {MAX_INSTALL_SECONDS}s', flush=True)
                next_report += 15
            time.sleep(1.0)

    install_details = INSTALL_LOG.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if exit_code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f'Matplotlib installation failed (pip exit code {exit_code}).\n'
            f'Installation log: {INSTALL_LOG}\n'
            f'Last installer messages:\n{install_details[-2500:]}\n'
            'Use Anaconda Prompt instead:\n'
            '  conda activate hydrogel-bioink\n'
            '  conda install -c conda-forge matplotlib\n'
            'Then restart the Jupyter kernel and Run All.'
        )
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    print('Matplotlib installation completed. Verifying imports and PNG renderer.', flush=True)
else:
    print('Matplotlib found: no package installation required.', flush=True)

try:

Helper functions¶

The helper functions below keep the notebook deterministic and restart-safe.

The most important principle is explicit input resolution. The notebook does not assume that a variable exists from an earlier Jupyter session. It checks that the required Phase 4 files are present, records their sizes and hashes, then uses those verified files for analysis.

In [8]:
def sha256_file(path: Path, block_size: int = 1024 * 1024) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(block_size), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def file_record(path: Path, role: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "canonical_filename": path.name,
        "relative_path": str(path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)) if path.exists() else "",
        "role": role,
        "exists": path.exists(),
        "file_size_bytes": path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else None,
        "sha256": sha256_file(path) if path.exists() else None,
        "status": "RESOLVED" if path.exists() else "MISSING",
    }


def require_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, required: Iterable[str], table_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    records = []
    for col in required:
        ok = col in df.columns
        records.append({
            "check": f"{table_name} has column {col}",
            "status": "PASS" if ok else "FAIL",
            "severity": "CRITICAL",
            "evidence": json.dumps({"column": col, "present": ok}),
        })
    return records


def safe_divide(num: pd.Series, den: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    num = pd.to_numeric(num, errors="coerce")
    den = pd.to_numeric(den, errors="coerce")
    return num.where(den != 0) / den.where(den != 0)


def loglog_slope(x: pd.Series, y: pd.Series) -> float:
    x = pd.to_numeric(x, errors="coerce")
    y = pd.to_numeric(y, errors="coerce")
    mask = (x > 0) & (y > 0) & np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    if int(mask.sum()) < 3:
        return np.nan
    lx = np.log10(x[mask].astype(float))
    ly = np.log10(y[mask].astype(float))
    if lx.nunique() < 2:
        return np.nan
    slope, _ = np.polyfit(lx, ly, 1)
    return float(slope)


def slope_label(slope: float) -> str:
    if pd.isna(slope):
        return "insufficient_positive_points"
    if slope < -0.15:
        return "screen_consistent_with_shear_thinning"
    if slope > 0.15:
        return "screen_consistent_with_viscosity_increase"
    return "screen_near_flat_on_loglog_axes"


def parse_rheology_source_label(source_stem: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Extract candidate label information from rheology filename stems.

    These fields are source-label descriptors only. They are not validated formulation entities.
    """
    text = "" if pd.isna(source_stem) else str(source_stem)
    alg = re.search(r"ALG[^_]*?(?:-I1G)?-?Ph_(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    ha = re.search(r"HA[^_]*?-?Ph_(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", text)
    temp = re.search(r"_(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)C(?:_|$)", text)
    replicate = re.search(r"_(\d+)$", text)
    return {
        "source_stem": text,
        "candidate_alg_ph_label": float(alg.group(1)) if alg else np.nan,
        "candidate_ha_ph_label": float(ha.group(1)) if ha else np.nan,
        "candidate_temperature_c_label": float(temp.group(1)) if temp else np.nan,
        "candidate_file_index_label": int(replicate.group(1)) if replicate else np.nan,
        "descriptor_status": "source_label_descriptor_only_not_validated_formulation",
    }


def write_csv(df: pd.DataFrame, filename: str) -> Path:
    path = PHASE5_DIR / filename
    df.to_csv(path, index=False)
    return path


PROGRESS_LOG = PHASE5_DIR / 'phase5_execution_progress.log'
PROGRESS_LOG.write_text('Phase 5 progress log — new clean-kernel run\n',encoding='utf-8')

def phase5_progress(message: str) -> None:
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')
    line=f'[{stamp}] {message}'
    with PROGRESS_LOG.open('a',encoding='utf-8') as fp:
        fp.write(line+'\n')
        fp.flush()
    print(line,flush=True)

def save_figure(fig: plt.Figure, filename: str) -> Path:
    """Save figures, close the Matplotlib object, but do NOT embed 25 full PNGs in the
    live Jupyter document. Rendering 25 embedded images can overload Jupyter's
    browser and make its progress indicator appear stuck on Windows.
    The PNG files are preserved, and a gallery is generated at the end.
    """
    path=FIGURE_DIR / filename
    phase5_progress('FIGURE START: '+filename)
    try:
        fig.savefig(path,dpi=145,bbox_inches='tight',facecolor='white')
    finally:
        plt.close(fig)
    phase5_progress('FIGURE FINISHED: '+filename+' | '+str(path.stat().st_size)+' bytes')
    return path

def row_count(path: Path) -> Optional[int]:
    if not path.exists() or path.suffix.lower() != ".csv":
        return None
    return sum(1 for _ in path.open("r", encoding="utf-8")) - 1

Validate Phase 5 input contracts¶

Before plotting, the notebook checks the fields it depends on. This keeps Phase 5 honest: if a future Phase 4 output changes shape, the notebook should fail early with a clear reason rather than quietly producing misleading figures.

In [12]:

validation_records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

], "measurement_point_linkage_layer.csv"))

    "linked_measurement_evidence_layer.csv": (len(linked), expected_counts.get("linked_measurement_evidence_layer.csv")),
    "measurement_point_linkage_layer.csv": (len(points), expected_counts.get("measurement_point_linkage_layer.csv")),

    "candidate_rheology_image_linkage.csv": (len(candidates), expected_counts.get("candidate_rheology_image_linkage.csv")),
}
for name, (observed, expected) in count_checks.items():
    ok = observed == expected
    validation_records.append({
        "check": f"{name} row count matches Phase 4 manifest",
        "status": "PASS" if ok else "FAIL",
        "severity": "CRITICAL",
        "evidence": json.dumps({"observed": int(observed), "expected": None if expected is None else int(expected)}),
    })

critical_phase4_failures = int(phase4_manifest.get("critical_validation_failures", -1))
validation_records.append({
    "check": "Phase 4 manifest reports zero critical validation failures",
    "status": "PASS" if critical_phase4_failures == 0 else "FAIL",
    "severity": "CRITICAL",
    "evidence": json.dumps({"critical_validation_failures": critical_phase4_failures}),
})

phase5_validation = pd.DataFrame(validation_records)
display(phase5_validation)

if ((phase5_validation["severity"] == "CRITICAL") & (phase5_validation["status"] != "PASS")).any():
    raise RuntimeError("Critical Phase 5 validation check failed. Review phase5_validation_summary.csv for details.")

Prepare analysis columns¶

This section creates numeric analysis columns and candidate source-label descriptors.

The descriptor extraction is deliberately cautious. The rheology filenames contain useful-looking labels, such as ALG-Ph and HA-Ph concentration tokens, but Phase 4 did not prove that those labels are validated formulation entities. Therefore Phase 5 labels them as candidate source-label descriptors, not confirmed formulations.

In [14]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: prepare numeric analysis fields")
points_analysis = points.copy()

numeric_cols = [
    "source_excel_row", "apparent_viscosity_source", "complex_viscosity_source", "frequency_hz", "loss_modulus_pa",
    "segment_time_s", "shear_rate_per_s", "shear_stress_pa", "storage_modulus_pa", "strain_fraction", "temperature_c", "time_s",
]
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in points_analysis.columns:
        points_analysis[col] = pd.to_numeric(points_analysis[col], errors="coerce")

label_records = [parse_rheology_source_label(stem) for stem in points_analysis["source_stem"].drop_duplicates().sort_values()]
source_label_descriptors = pd.DataFrame(label_records)
points_analysis = points_analysis.merge(source_label_descriptors, on="source_stem", how="left")

points_analysis["tan_delta"] = safe_divide(points_analysis["loss_modulus_pa"], points_analysis["storage_modulus_pa"])
points_analysis["has_point_qc_flag"] = points_analysis["point_qc_finding_ids"].notna() & (points_analysis["point_qc_finding_ids"].astype(str).str.strip() != "")
points_analysis["positive_apparent_viscosity_for_log_plot"] = (points_analysis["apparent_viscosity_source"] > 0) & (points_analysis["shear_rate_per_s"] > 0)
points_analysis["positive_moduli_for_log_plot"] = (points_analysis["strain_fraction"] > 0) & (points_analysis["storage_modulus_pa"] > 0) & (points_analysis["loss_modulus_pa"] > 0)

source_label_path = write_csv(source_label_descriptors, "phase5_candidate_source_label_descriptors.csv")
print("Candidate source-label descriptor rows:", len(source_label_descriptors))
display(source_label_descriptors.head(10))

Measurement-family coverage¶

The first useful Phase 5 question is simple: what measurement families are present, and which columns are populated?

This matters because viscosity and oscillatory moduli are different rheological tests. They should not be blended into one response variable just because both came from a rheometer.

In [16]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: measurement family coverage")
coverage_rows = []
analysis_fields = [
    "shear_rate_per_s", "apparent_viscosity_source", "complex_viscosity_source", "storage_modulus_pa", "loss_modulus_pa",
    "strain_fraction", "frequency_hz", "temperature_c", "tan_delta",
]
for family, group in points_analysis.groupby("measurement_family", dropna=False):
    row = {
        "measurement_family": family,
        "measurement_point_rows": len(group),
        "unique_worksheets": group["worksheet_key"].nunique(dropna=True),
        "unique_source_stems": group["source_stem"].nunique(dropna=True),
        "rows_with_qc_flags": int(group["has_point_qc_flag"].sum()),
        "candidate_linkage_rows": int((group["phase4_linkage_status"] == "candidate_by_matching_source_stem").sum()),
        "unresolved_or_not_one_to_one_rows": int((group["phase4_linkage_status"] != "candidate_by_matching_source_stem").sum()),
    }
    for field in analysis_fields:
        row[f"{field}_non_null"] = int(group[field].notna().sum()) if field in group else 0
    coverage_rows.append(row)

measurement_family_summary = pd.DataFrame(coverage_rows).sort_values("measurement_family")
measurement_family_path = write_csv(measurement_family_summary, "phase5_measurement_family_summary.csv")
display(measurement_family_summary)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.5))
counts = points_analysis["measurement_family"].value_counts().sort_index()
ax.bar(counts.index.astype(str), counts.values, color=["#4477AA", "#66A61E"][:len(counts)])
ax.set_ylabel("Measurement-point rows")
ax.set_xlabel("Measurement family")
ax.set_title("Phase 5 measurement-point coverage by rheology family")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=20)
for i, v in enumerate(counts.values):
    ax.text(i, v, f"{v:,}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9)
fig.tight_layout()
family_fig_path = save_figure(fig, "phase5_measurement_family_counts.png")
family_fig_path

Steady-shear viscosity exploration¶

Steady-shear viscosity is plotted against shear rate. If viscosity decreases as shear rate increases, that is a screen for shear-thinning behaviour. However, the source token mPas remains unresolved, and nonpositive apparent-viscosity values are retained as QC-warning context rather than forced into a log plot.

The log-log slope calculated below is an exploratory screening statistic per worksheet. It is not a fitted constitutive model and not a production materials descriptor.

In [18]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: steady shear curves")
viscosity_points = points_analysis.loc[points_analysis["measurement_family"] == "steady_shear_viscosity"].copy()

viscosity_summary_rows = []
for worksheet_key, group in viscosity_points.groupby("worksheet_key", dropna=False):
    slope = loglog_slope(group["shear_rate_per_s"], group["apparent_viscosity_source"])
    positive_mask = (group["shear_rate_per_s"] > 0) & (group["apparent_viscosity_source"] > 0)
    viscosity_summary_rows.append({
        "worksheet_key": worksheet_key,
        "source_stem": group["source_stem"].iloc[0] if len(group) else None,
        "member_path": group["member_path"].iloc[0] if len(group) else None,
        "measurement_points": len(group),
        "positive_log_plot_points": int(positive_mask.sum()),
        "qc_flagged_points": int(group["has_point_qc_flag"].sum()),
        "shear_rate_min_per_s": group["shear_rate_per_s"].min(),
        "shear_rate_max_per_s": group["shear_rate_per_s"].max(),
        "apparent_viscosity_min_source_token": group["apparent_viscosity_source"].min(),
        "apparent_viscosity_median_source_token": group["apparent_viscosity_source"].median(),
        "apparent_viscosity_max_source_token": group["apparent_viscosity_source"].max(),
        "loglog_slope_viscosity_vs_shear_rate": slope,
        "slope_screen_interpretation": slope_label(slope),
        "viscosity_unit_status": group["viscosity_unit_status"].dropna().iloc[0] if group["viscosity_unit_status"].notna().any() else "mPas token unresolved",
        "analysis_caution": "exploratory_screen_only; source token mPas not converted; nonpositive values retained outside log plot",
    })

viscosity_curve_summary = pd.DataFrame(viscosity_summary_rows).sort_values(["source_stem", "worksheet_key"])
viscosity_path = write_csv(viscosity_curve_summary, "phase5_viscosity_curve_screening_summary.csv")
display(viscosity_curve_summary.head(12))

vis_plot = viscosity_points.loc[viscosity_points["positive_apparent_viscosity_for_log_plot"]].copy()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.5))
if not vis_plot.empty:
    for _, group in vis_plot.groupby("worksheet_key"):
        group = group.sort_values("shear_rate_per_s")
        ax.plot(group["shear_rate_per_s"], group["apparent_viscosity_source"], alpha=0.28, linewidth=0.9)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("Shear rate / s$^{-1}$")
ax.set_ylabel("Apparent viscosity, source token `mPas` unresolved")
ax.set_title("Exploratory steady-shear viscosity curves")
ax.grid(True, which="both", linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.35)
fig.tight_layout()
vis_fig_path = save_figure(fig, "phase5_viscosity_vs_shear_rate_loglog.png")

print("Steady-shear rows:", len(viscosity_points))
print("Rows included in log-log plot:", len(vis_plot))
print("Rows excluded from log-log plot because shear rate or viscosity was nonpositive/missing:", len(viscosity_points) - len(vis_plot))
vis_fig_path

Oscillatory moduli exploration¶

For oscillatory data, Phase 5 plots storage modulus G′ and loss modulus G″ against strain fraction. In this dataset, the Phase 4 measurement-point table reports frequency as 1 Hz for the oscillatory rows, so the main visible axis is strain.

tan δ = G″/G′ is calculated only where G′ is nonzero. This ratio can describe relative viscous versus elastic response, but Phase 5 does not use it to claim gelation, LVR selection or printability.

In [20]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: oscillatory mechanical curves")
moduli_points = points_analysis.loc[points_analysis["measurement_family"] == "oscillatory_moduli"].copy()

moduli_summary_rows = []
for worksheet_key, group in moduli_points.groupby("worksheet_key", dropna=False):
    positive_mask = (group["strain_fraction"] > 0) & (group["storage_modulus_pa"] > 0) & (group["loss_modulus_pa"] > 0)
    gprime_gt_gdouble = (group["storage_modulus_pa"] > group["loss_modulus_pa"]) & group["storage_modulus_pa"].notna() & group["loss_modulus_pa"].notna()
    moduli_summary_rows.append({
        "worksheet_key": worksheet_key,
        "source_stem": group["source_stem"].iloc[0] if len(group) else None,
        "member_path": group["member_path"].iloc[0] if len(group) else None,
        "measurement_points": len(group),
        "positive_log_plot_points": int(positive_mask.sum()),
        "qc_flagged_points": int(group["has_point_qc_flag"].sum()),
        "frequency_hz_unique_count": group["frequency_hz"].nunique(dropna=True),
        "frequency_hz_min": group["frequency_hz"].min(),
        "frequency_hz_max": group["frequency_hz"].max(),
        "strain_fraction_min": group["strain_fraction"].min(),
        "strain_fraction_median": group["strain_fraction"].median(),
        "strain_fraction_max": group["strain_fraction"].max(),
        "storage_modulus_pa_median": group["storage_modulus_pa"].median(),
        "loss_modulus_pa_median": group["loss_modulus_pa"].median(),
        "tan_delta_median": group["tan_delta"].median(),
        "fraction_points_gprime_above_gdoubleprime": float(gprime_gt_gdouble.mean()) if len(group) else np.nan,
        "analysis_caution": "exploratory_summary_only; no LVR selection or gelation threshold inferred",
    })

moduli_curve_summary = pd.DataFrame(moduli_summary_rows).sort_values(["source_stem", "worksheet_key"])
moduli_path = write_csv(moduli_curve_summary, "phase5_moduli_curve_screening_summary.csv")
display(moduli_curve_summary.head(12))

mod_plot = moduli_points.loc[moduli_points["positive_moduli_for_log_plot"]].copy()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.5))
if not mod_plot.empty:
    for _, group in mod_plot.groupby("worksheet_key"):
        group = group.sort_values("strain_fraction")
        ax.plot(group["strain_fraction"], group["storage_modulus_pa"], color="#4477AA", alpha=0.22, linewidth=0.8)
        ax.plot(group["strain_fraction"], group["loss_modulus_pa"], color="#CC6677", alpha=0.22, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("Strain fraction")
ax.set_ylabel("Modulus / Pa")
ax.set_title("Exploratory oscillatory moduli curves: G′ and G″ versus strain")
ax.grid(True, which="both", linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.35)
ax.plot([], [], color="#4477AA", label="G′ storage modulus")
ax.plot([], [], color="#CC6677", label="G″ loss modulus")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
moduli_fig_path = save_figure(fig, "phase5_moduli_vs_strain_loglog.png")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5))
tan_plot = moduli_points.loc[(moduli_points["strain_fraction"] > 0) & (moduli_points["tan_delta"] > 0)].copy()
if not tan_plot.empty:
    ax.scatter(tan_plot["strain_fraction"], tan_plot["tan_delta"], s=11, alpha=0.35, color="#228833", edgecolors="none")
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("Strain fraction")
ax.set_ylabel("tan δ = G″ / G′")
ax.set_title("Exploratory tan δ distribution across oscillatory points")
ax.grid(True, which="both", linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.35)
fig.tight_layout()
tan_fig_path = save_figure(fig, "phase5_tan_delta_vs_strain.png")

print("Oscillatory rows:", len(moduli_points))
print("Rows included in moduli log-log plot:", len(mod_plot))
moduli_fig_path, tan_fig_path

phase5_progress("SECTION FINISHED: oscillatory mechanical curves")

Candidate formulation-label coverage¶

This section summarises candidate source-label descriptors extracted from rheology filenames. It is useful for planning Phase 5 comparisons, but it is not a validated formulation table.

The reason for this caution is subtle but important: a filename label may reflect intended composition, instrument export name, file naming habit or processing condition. Without explicit source documentation, it should not be promoted into a confirmed formulation entity.

In [22]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: candidate formulation label coverage")
source_level = points_analysis.drop_duplicates("source_stem").copy()
source_level["candidate_alg_ph_label_reported"] = source_level["candidate_alg_ph_label"].notna()
source_level["candidate_ha_ph_label_reported"] = source_level["candidate_ha_ph_label"].notna()

candidate_formulation_summary = (
    source_level
    .groupby(["candidate_alg_ph_label", "candidate_ha_ph_label"], dropna=False)
    .agg(
        candidate_source_stems=("source_stem", "nunique"),
        measurement_point_rows=("source_stem", lambda s: int(points_analysis.loc[points_analysis["source_stem"].isin(s), "measurement_point_key"].nunique())),
        source_stem_examples=("source_stem", lambda s: "; ".join(list(s.astype(str).head(4)))),
    )
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values(["candidate_alg_ph_label", "candidate_ha_ph_label"], na_position="last")
)
candidate_formulation_summary["interpretation_status"] = "candidate_source_label_descriptor_only_not_validated_formulation"
formulation_path = write_csv(candidate_formulation_summary, "phase5_candidate_formulation_label_summary.csv")
display(candidate_formulation_summary.head(20))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 5.2))
plot_df = source_level.copy()
mask = plot_df["candidate_alg_ph_label"].notna() | plot_df["candidate_ha_ph_label"].notna()
plot_df = plot_df.loc[mask]
if not plot_df.empty:
    x = plot_df["candidate_alg_ph_label"].fillna(-0.1)
    y = plot_df["candidate_ha_ph_label"].fillna(-0.1)
    ax.scatter(x, y, s=50, alpha=0.65, color="#AA3377")
ax.set_xlabel("Candidate ALG-Ph label from source stem; -0.1 means absent")
ax.set_ylabel("Candidate HA-Ph label from source stem; -0.1 means absent")
ax.set_title("Candidate source-label descriptor coverage")
ax.grid(True, linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.35)
fig.tight_layout()
formulation_fig_path = save_figure(fig, "phase5_candidate_source_label_coverage.png")
formulation_fig_path

Image metadata context¶

Phase 5 can describe image metadata coverage because Phase 4 linked the standardised image metadata back to raw image_index.csv identifiers.

This remains metadata analysis. The physical image files are not inspected here. Image-file integrity, dimensions, colour mode and simple computer-vision features belong in the optional Phase 6 image-file audit.

In [24]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: image-index summary")
images_analysis = images.copy()
images_analysis["intensity_numeric"] = pd.to_numeric(images_analysis["intensity"], errors="coerce")

summary_parts = []
for field in ["shape", "ink_type_ph", "intensity", "contain_sps", "completeness_sam", "image_file_audit_status", "rheology_linkage_status"]:
    counts = images_analysis[field].fillna("<missing>").astype(str).value_counts(dropna=False).reset_index()
    counts.columns = ["value", "record_count"]
    counts.insert(0, "field", field)
    summary_parts.append(counts)
image_metadata_summary = pd.concat(summary_parts, ignore_index=True)
image_metadata_summary["interpretation_note"] = "image metadata summary only; physical image files not audited in Phase 5"
image_summary_path = write_csv(image_metadata_summary, "phase5_image_metadata_descriptive_summary.csv")
display(image_metadata_summary.head(30))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.8))
shape_counts = images_analysis["shape"].fillna("<missing>").value_counts().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax.bar(shape_counts.index.astype(str), shape_counts.values, color="#228833")

QC and unresolved-boundary summary¶

This section keeps the “messy but scientifically important” records visible. The analysis should not hide nonpositive rheology values, unresolved units, missing image annotations or deferred physical-sample entities.

For Phase 5, these are not annoying leftovers. They are the guard rails.

Expanded exploratory visualisation atlas — how to read it¶

The figures below are descriptive evidence, not fitted material-design models. A measurement point is not an independent formulation, and a worksheet is not automatically an independent physical sample. We show many views to reveal limitations as well as scientific structure.

  • A logarithmic rheology plot uses positive finite measurements only. The excluded and QC-flagged observations are counted separately; they are never quietly removed from the underlying data.
  • The apparent-viscosity source token mPas has unresolved unit meaning. We therefore make no conversion into Pa·s and no cross-study magnitude comparison.
  • The oscillatory test has fixed recorded frequency = 1 Hz; therefore plots of G′, G″ and tan δ use the recorded strain axis. They are not frequency sweeps. The field strain_fraction follows the Phase 4 schema but requires confirmation of the original instrument convention before physical strain-based thresholds are interpreted.
  • Source filename tokens ALG-Ph and HA-Ph are candidate labels, not verified concentration/composition measurements. Image labels are image-index metadata, with no confirmed sample-level correspondence to the rheology files.
  • Small-multiple curves are chosen deterministically by source filename to illustrate shape variation; they are not representative estimates of a larger population.
In [28]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: extended plotting helpers")
# Phase 5 extended plotting helpers and independent-observation summaries
ADDITIONAL_FIGURES = []
ADDITIONAL_TABLES = []

def store_plot(fig, stem: str):
    name = f'phase5_{stem}.png'
    path = save_figure(fig, name)
    ADDITIONAL_FIGURES.append('figures/' + name)
    return path

def store_table(frame: pd.DataFrame, name: str) -> Path:
    filename = 'phase5_' + name + '.csv'
    path = write_csv(frame, filename)
    ADDITIONAL_TABLES.append(filename)
    return path

def no_data(ax, reason='Insufficient comparable records'):
    ax.text(.5,.5,reason,ha='center',va='center',transform=ax.transAxes)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])

def numeric_positive(df, x, y):
    mask = np.isfinite(df[x]) & np.isfinite(df[y]) & (df[x]>0) & (df[y]>0)
    return df.loc[mask].copy()

def tidy_axes(ax, logx=False, logy=False):
    if logx: ax.set_xscale('log')
    if logy: ax.set_yscale('log')
    ax.grid(True,which='major',alpha=.2,linewidth=.6)

# Each worksheet is counted once; measurement-point counts refer to nested rows.
worksheet_stats = (points_analysis.groupby(['worksheet_key','measurement_family'],dropna=False)
    .agg(source_stem=('source_stem','first'), point_rows=('measurement_point_key','nunique'),
         flagged_points=('has_point_qc_flag','sum'),
         candidate_linkage=('phase4_linkage_status','first'))
    .reset_index())
store_table(worksheet_stats, 'worksheet_level_evidence_summary')

# Numeric value completeness per measurement family (not global percent).
cols = ['shear_rate_per_s','apparent_viscosity_source','shear_stress_pa',
        'strain_fraction','storage_modulus_pa','loss_modulus_pa',
        'complex_viscosity_source','frequency_hz','temperature_c','time_s']
coverage_long=[]
for family, g in points_analysis.groupby('measurement_family'):
    for field in cols:
        coverage_long.append({'measurement_family':family,'field':field,
                              'measurement_point_rows':len(g),
                              'non_null_count':int(g[field].notna().sum()),
                              'completeness_pct':round(100*g[field].notna().mean(),2)})
field_completeness=pd.DataFrame(coverage_long)
store_table(field_completeness,'field_completeness_by_family')

fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.5),layout='constrained')
for ax,(fam,g) in zip(axes, worksheet_stats.groupby('measurement_family')):
    vals=g.point_rows.value_counts().sort_index()
    ax.bar(vals.index.astype(str),vals.values,color='#4779A9')
    ax.set_title(f'{fam.replace("_"," ")} — {len(g)} worksheets')
    ax.set_xlabel('Measurement points per worksheet')
    ax.set_ylabel('Worksheets')
    tidy_axes(ax)
store_plot(fig,'worksheet_point_counts')

mat=field_completeness.pivot(index='field',columns='measurement_family',values='completeness_pct')
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,5.6),layout='constrained')
a=ax.imshow(mat.values,aspect='auto',vmin=0,vmax=100,cmap='Blues')
ax.set_xticks(range(len(mat.columns)),[x.replace('_',' ') for x in mat.columns],rotation=12)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(mat.index)),mat.index)
for (r,c),v in np.ndenumerate(mat.values):
    ax.text(c,r,f'{v:.0f}%',ha='center',va='center',color='white' if v>65 else 'black',fontsize=9)
ax.set_title('Field completeness by rheology family (not pooled)')
fig.colorbar(a,ax=ax,shrink=.8,label='Non-missing rows (%)')
store_plot(fig,'measurement_field_completeness_heatmap')

Steady shear — viscosity, flow curves and quality exclusions¶

When a viscosity curve falls as shear rate increases, it is consistent with shear-thinning over that measured range. The log–log slope is an exploratory screen, not a fitted constitutive-law parameter or a guaranteed demonstration of extrusion printability. Plotting stress against shear rate adds a complementary flow-curve view. Negative or zero readings cannot be shown on log axes and are counted explicitly.

Oscillatory mechanics — G′, G″ and the loss tangent¶

Storage modulus G′ describes recoverable (elastic) response; loss modulus G″ describes dissipative (viscous) response under oscillatory loading. tan δ = G″ / G′ describes their relative balance at each measurement point. The line tan δ = 1 means G′ and G″ are equal at that particular measured strain, not a validated gel point. Determining a linear viscoelastic region (LVR) requires a separately justified method and instrument-condition review.

In [32]:
phase5_progress("SECTION START: oscillatory mechanics atlas")
osc=moduli_points.copy()
osc['positive_moduli']=(np.isfinite(osc.storage_modulus_pa)&np.isfinite(osc.loss_modulus_pa)&
                        (osc.storage_modulus_pa>0)&(osc.loss_modulus_pa>0))
osc['modulus_balance']=np.where(osc.storage_modulus_pa>osc.loss_modulus_pa,'G-prime > G-double-prime',
                                 np.where(osc.storage_modulus_pa<osc.loss_modulus_pa,'G-prime < G-double-prime','G-prime = G-double-prime'))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5,5.5),layout='constrained')
g=osc.loc[osc.positive_moduli]
if len(g):
    ax.scatter(g.storage_modulus_pa,g.loss_modulus_pa,s=9,alpha=.4,color='#4477AA')
    lower=max(min(g.storage_modulus_pa.min(),g.loss_modulus_pa.min()),1e-10)
    upper=max(g.storage_modulus_pa.max(),g.loss_modulus_pa.max())
    ax.plot([lower,upper],[lower,upper],linestyle='--',lw=1.5,color='#BB5566',label='G′ = G″')
    tidy_axes(ax,logx=True,logy=True);ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.set(title='Elastic and viscous contributions at measured points',
       xlabel='Storage modulus G′ (Pa)',ylabel='Loss modulus G″ (Pa)')
store_plot(fig,'storage_vs_loss_modulus_scatter')

balance_counts=osc.modulus_balance.value_counts().sort_index()
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4.6),layout='constrained')
ax.barh(balance_counts.index.astype(str),balance_counts.values,color='#4477AA')

    .agg(source_stem=('source_stem','first'),median_tan_delta=('tan_delta','median'),
         median_gprime_pa=('storage_modulus_pa','median'),median_gdoubleprime_pa=('loss_modulus_pa','median'),
         flagged_points=('has_point_qc_flag','sum'),rows=('measurement_point_key','nunique'))
    .reset_index())
store_table(osc_curve,'oscillatory_worksheet_statistics')

vals=osc_curve.median_tan_delta.replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna()
if len(vals):
    ax.hist(vals,bins=min(15,max(5,len(vals)//2)),color='#228833',edgecolor='white')
    ax.axvline(1,ls='--',color='#CC6677',label='tan δ = 1');ax.legend(frameon=False)
else:no_data(ax)

chosen=(osc.loc[osc.positive_moduli].groupby('source_stem',dropna=True)
    .filter(lambda z: len(z)>=5).source_stem.drop_duplicates().sort_values().head(6).tolist())
fig,axes=plt.subplots(2,3,figsize=(14,8.5),layout='constrained')
for ax,stem in zip(axes.flat,chosen):
    z=osc.loc[(osc.source_stem==stem)&osc.positive_moduli&(osc.strain_fraction>0)].sort_values('strain_fraction')
    for _,ws in z.groupby('worksheet_key'):
        ax.plot(ws.strain_fraction,ws.storage_modulus_pa,color='#4477AA',lw=1)
        ax.plot(ws.strain_fraction,ws.loss_modulus_pa,color='#CC6677',lw=1)
    tidy_axes(ax,logx=True,logy=True)
    ax.set(title=stem[:46],xlabel='Recorded strain field (convention to verify)',ylabel='Modulus (Pa)')
for ax in list(axes.flat)[len(chosen):]:no_data(ax)
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
fig.legend(handles=[Line2D([],[],color='#4477AA',label='G′'),Line2D([],[],color='#CC6677',label='G″')],
           loc='lower center',ncol=2,frameon=False)
fig.suptitle('Six illustrative oscillatory source stems — no LVR inferred',fontsize=13)
store_plot(fig,'oscillatory_example_curve_small_multiples')

# Frequency does NOT vary: show the observed instrument field and avoid false frequency sweep.
freq_values=osc.frequency_hz.dropna()
print('Recorded oscillatory frequencies:',sorted(freq_values.unique().tolist()))
assert freq_values.nunique()==1 and np.isclose(float(freq_values.iloc[0]),1), 'Reassess the frequency-sweep interpretation if this changes.'

Data quality, provenance and linkage — what limits a prediction model?¶

The modelling unit must be a verified formulation or physical sample, not one point along a rheology curve. Here we visualise QC prevalence and filename-stem pairings at the appropriate levels. A candidate one-to-one pair of files does not establish that they are measurements from one physical sample. In future ML, grouping train/test splits by independent sample or formulation would be essential to avoid leakage.

In [34]:

Printing-context metadata — categorical and temporal coverage¶

The image index records geometry labels, formulation-like strings and irradiation-intensity tokens. These are not validated specimen measurements, print-quality scores, or confirmed material-performance targets. Missing SPS/completeness annotations are shown as missing, never silently interpreted as “no”. Dates refer to recorded image-index metadata, not necessarily independent print trials.

Exploratory interpretation and next-stage decision boundary¶

Data science: the complete evidence chain lets us produce repeatable descriptive tables, worksheet-grouped curves, QC audits and provenance. The current source does not establish independent sample IDs, validated structure/composition predictors or ground-truth printability labels. Supervised regression or classification of printability would therefore be premature.

Polymer science: a shear-thinning screen may help formulate future extrusion questions, while G′, G″ and tan δ help describe elastic and viscous behaviour. But neither by itself establishes a printability window. Interpreting any concentration–rheology trend requires verified formulation composition and sample linkage; it cannot be inferred from naming conventions.

Reproducibility: the input manifest preserves hashes and row counts. Figure filenames and source tables are generated in a deterministic order. With the documented Python environment selected, the notebook can be closed, reopened, restarted and run top-to-bottom without any hidden in-memory variables.

Write data dictionary, validation ledger, README summary and run manifest¶

The final cell writes the Phase 5 documentation outputs. This makes the notebook useful as a GitHub checkpoint: a reviewer can see the code, the tables, the figures, and the stated scientific boundaries.

    "severity": "CRITICAL",
    "evidence": json.dumps({"path": str(manifest_path), "size_bytes": manifest_path.stat().st_size if manifest_path.exists() else None}),
})
phase5_validation = pd.DataFrame(validation_records)
validation_path = write_csv(phase5_validation, "phase5_validation_summary.csv")
critical_failures = int(((phase5_validation["severity"] == "CRITICAL") & (phase5_validation["status"] != "PASS")).sum())

# Update manifest with final validation count.
manifest["validation_counts"] = phase5_validation["status"].value_counts(dropna=False).to_dict()
manifest["critical_validation_failures"] = critical_failures
manifest["output_row_counts"]["phase5_validation_summary.csv"] = row_count(validation_path)
manifest["output_sha256"]["phase5_validation_summary.csv"] = sha256_file(validation_path)
manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")


# Small inline preview selection for immediate feedback; other figures available
# in phase5_figure_gallery.html (open in a browser next to the figures folder).
phase5_progress('PREVIEWS START: four selected figures')
for preview in [
    'phase5_viscosity_vs_shear_rate_loglog.png',
    'phase5_moduli_vs_strain_loglog.png',
    'phase5_measurement_field_completeness_heatmap.png',
    'phase5_image_shape_intensity_heatmap.png'
]:
    picture=FIGURE_DIR / preview
    if picture.is_file():
        print('Preview:',preview,flush=True)
        display(Image(filename=str(picture),width=520))
phase5_progress('PREVIEWS FINISHED: all figures are saved; offline gallery ready')
print("Phase 5 outputs written to:", PHASE5_DIR)
print("Critical validation failures:", critical_failures)
display(phase5_validation.tail(20))

if critical_failures:
    raise RuntimeError("Critical Phase 5 validation failures were recorded.")

phase5_progress("SECTION FINISHED: manifest and validation ledger")
